title_bis: Pinakamaayo nga Materyales para sa Proteksyon sa
fact_en: Soft, thick materials like cotton, cloth, and foam reduce sound better than hard or thin materials because they absorb more sound waves.
fact_bis: Ang humok ug baga nga mga materyales sama sa cotton, panapton, ug foam mas makapamenos sa tingog kaysa gahi o nipis nga mga materyales tungod kay mas ma-absorb nila ang mga sound wave.
evidence: Title ends on a bare particle with its head noun missing.

fact_en:
How many ants are there for every person?

There are about 2.5 million ants for every single person on Earth — that adds up to roughly twenty quadrillion ants in total!
fact_bis:
Pila ka hulmigas ang naa para sa matag tawo?

Adunay mga 2.5 milyon nga hulmigas para sa matag usa ka tawo sa kalibutan — moabot kini sa mga baynte ka quadrillion nga hulmigas!
evidence: In Cebuano langgam means BIRD, not ant; the card's own body says hulmigas, so the headline reads "Birds Per Person" over a card about ants.

fact_en:
What's the difference between a vaccine and medicine?

A vaccine is given BEFORE you get sick to protect you, while medicine is taken when you're already sick to make you better.
fact_bis:
Unsay kalainan sa bakuna ug tambal?

Ang bakuna gihatag SA WALA pa ka magsakit aron manalipod nimo, samtang ang tambal giinom kon nagsakit na ka aron mamaayo.
evidence: Cebuano gamot means ROOT (medicine is tambal, which the body uses throughout), so the title reads as a garbled "vaccine without root" on a vaccine-vs-medicine card.

fact_en: Scabies can be treated with a special medicine or cream that a doctor prescribes.
fact_bis: Ang galis matambalan gamit ang espesyal nga tambal o cream nga ihatag sa doktor.
evidence: "Gamot sa Galis" reads in Cebuano as "root/root-cause of scabies" rather than its medicine, and the body itself uses tambal.

fact_en:
Why do we sweat?

We sweat to cool down—as sweat evaporates from our skin, it carries heat away and lowers our body temperature!
fact_bis:
Nganong mosingot ta?

Mosingot ta aron mobugnaw: samtang mo-alisngaw ang singot sa panit, gikuha niini ang kainit, mao nga mokunhod ang temperatura sa lawas!
evidence: Bahu is ODOUR in Cebuano, so the title says smell cools the body, while the card (and its body word singot) is about sweat.

fact_en:
Why does this monkey have cheek pouches?

This monkey stores food in its cheek pouches while it keeps searching for more to eat!
fact_bis:
Nganong adunay supot sa aping kining unggoya?

Gitagoan sa kining unggoya ang pagkaon sa supot sa aping niini samtang nangita pa kini og dugang!
evidence: Ungo is a witch/aswang in Cebuano, not unggoy (monkey) as the body correctly has it — a child reads "cheek pouch of the monster".

fact_en: This monkey is active during the day and sleeps at night!
fact_bis: Kini nga unggoy aktibo kon adlaw ug matulog kon gabii!
evidence: Same ungo (witch) for unggoy (monkey) swap; the body says unggoy, so the headline names a folklore monster active by day.

fact_en:
Can rest alone cure TB?

No — rest and good food help, but only the proper medicine can actually kill the TB bacteria and cure it.
fact_bis:
Makaayo ba ang pahulay lang sa TB?

Dili — maayo ang pahulay ug masustansiyang pagkaon, apan dili niini mapatay ang bakterya sa TB, ang husto nga tambal ra ang makaayo niini.
evidence: "Gamot Batok sa TB" reads as "root against TB" in Cebuano; the body uses tambal, the correct Cebuano word for medicine.

fact_en: Many ants build underground nests with tunnels and chambers, where they store food and take care of their eggs.
fact_bis: Daghang hulmigas ang naghimo og pugad ilalom sa yuta nga adunay mga tunel ug lawak diin gitipigan ang pagkaon ug giatiman ang mga itlog.
evidence: "Salag sa Langgam" is a BIRD's nest in Cebuano, but the card and its body (hulmigas, pugad) are about ant nests.

fact_en: Aphids love crowding onto soft new shoots and young leaves, where the sap is sweetest.
fact_bis: Ganahan magpundok ang mga aphid sa humok nga bag-ong saha ug linghod nga dahon nga puno sa duga.
evidence: Lumot is MOSS in Cebuano; the card is about soft new shoots, which its own body renders correctly as humok nga bag-ong saha.

fact_en: Ants live together in huge groups called colonies.
fact_bis: Ang mga hulmigas nagpuyo nga tingob sa dagkong grupo nga gitawag og kolonya.
evidence: "Kolonya sa Langgam" reads as a bird colony; the body uses hulmigas for the ants the card is actually about.

fact_en: The leaves of the lagundi plant are usually used as medicine — boiled or made into an extract!
fact_bis: Ang mga dahon sa lagundi ang kasagarang gigamit isip tambal — lat-an o kuhaan og katas!
evidence: Worst of the gamot set: the card's whole point is that the LEAVES are used, yet the Cebuano title says "leaves as ROOT" where the body says tambal.
